claims.statement: The toolchain capability model (src/shared/toolchains/types.ts) defines a fixed set (shell.bash, vcs.git, js.node, python.*, search.*, data.jq, network.curl) with providers project/custom/system/bundled/managed/legacy-upstream-managed, per-capability preferences, ToolHealth states, and a closed TOOLCHAIN_* error code set.

ToolchainManager (src/main/toolchains/manager.ts) collects executable seeds from custom/system/bundled/managed/legacy sources, probes each, normalizes/dedupes candidates, selects defaults, and produces a ToolchainSnapshot carrying revision, platform, arch, candidates, defaults)SkipPress and publicState.

The runtime catalog schema (src/shared/toolchains/catalog-schema.ts, version 2) requires per-platform/arch variants with url, sha256, downloadBytes, archive format, and installer id; the app ships two signed catalogs plus the current target's core search tools as extra resources.

ManagedComponentInstaller (src/main/toolchains/installer.ts) runs a phase machine and verifies every download byte-by-byte against the catalog sha256 before extraction, writes a signed runtime manifest, and resumes partial downloads by re-verifying the existing archive.
Component removal renames the component tree to a staging trash path before deleting and is refused while an agent command is running or an install is active (manager.ts).

Toolchain profiles (javascript-essentials, python-essentials, windows-shell-essentials, cli-essentials) map to managed component sets, and caches (npm, uv, bun, downloads) are enumerable and clearable.

The Agent Host's toolchain-runtime.ts applies the pushed ToolchainSnapshot, rejects older revisions, caches per-request resolutions keyed by cwd/intent/trusted/revision, and refetches when a resolution's inventory revision is stale.

createExecutionContext in toolchain-runtime.ts assembles a ToolExecutionContext (nativeEnv, shellEnv, per-capability CommandDescriptors with envPatch/shellEnvPatch and cwdSemantics) used to spawn agent bash/git/node processes.
Toolchain execution intent requests are only trusted when they come from the app-owned Host path; a Renderer cannot request a trusted project resolution.
The user can select custom tools per capability (choose-custom-tool) and set preferences (set-preference, auto/system/bundled/managed/custom) through the ToolchainActionRequest surface.
